publications.title: Navigation ability is associated with video game experience and GPS use, but not with other everyday spatial activities
publications.summary: N = 258 completed questionnaire of everyday spatial activities. Measured small-scale spatial abilities, like mental rotation, and large-scale spatial ability (navigation) in desktop and immersive VR. Video game experience positively correlated with spatial ability, GPS use negatively correlated with spatial ability.

publications.title: Measurement of spatial ability: Reevaluating and revising measures of mental rotation
publications.summary: Item response theory analyses of three mental rotation tests (Flags, Mental Rotations Test, Revised PSVT:R). Best items combined into a 35-item hybrid test. One general mental rotation ability, no separate ability for 2-D vs. 3-D figures. Hybrid test reliable across a wide range of ability.

publications.title: Wayfinding strategies in an outdoor environment: Effects of global landmarks, configural knowledge, and spatial anxiety
publications.summary: Participants learned an outdoor route; directing attention to a distant mountain range did not change wayfinding strategies. Better configural knowledge and lower spatial anxiety predicted shortcutting. Spatial anxiety mediated sex differences in strategy use.

publications.title: Systematically reviewing the rigour of immersive virtual reality research in STEM education: a deep dive into threats to internal validity
publications.venue: Journal of Computer Assisted Learning 42 (1), e70165
publications.summary: Systematic review of 44 studies comparing immersive VR with conventional instruction in STEM (2013–2023), rated on 13 internal validity controls. No study met all 13, average of 5.36 control issues. Missing method details were a major problem.

publications.title: Confounded or controlled? A systematic review of media comparison studies involving immersive virtual reality for STEM education
publications.summary: Systematic review of 38 studies comparing immersive VR with conventional instruction in STEM (2013–2022). Only 26% of comparisons fully controlled on instructional method and content, 40% had at least one confound.

publications.title: Stress affects navigation strategies in immersive virtual reality
publications.summary: N = 48 learned a maze in immersive VR, then navigated under control or high-stress conditions (blocked paths, darkness, fog, time limit). Stress reduced shortcutting and navigation efficiency. Higher trait spatial anxiety related to more stress and less efficient navigation.

publications.title: Visualizing cross-sections of 3D objects: Developing efficient measures using item response theory
publications.summary: N = 498 completed three tests of visualizing cross-sections of 3-D objects. Two tests measured one general cross-sectioning ability; item response theory used to combine their most informative items into an efficient test. Geology-based test too difficult. No sex or ethnicity differences after controls.

publications.title: Large-scale vs small-scale spatial abilities: Development of a broad spatial activities questionnaire
publications.venue: Proceedings of the annual meeting of the Cognitive Science Society 44 (44)
publications.summary: Updated Spatial Activities Questionnaire by adding navigation-related hobbies and video games. Principal component analysis found five components. Navigation component correlated with sense of direction and childhood wayfinding experience, no sex difference.
